boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Kessler's Cross Lanes record (August 26, 1861) in Operations in Western Virginia [June-December 1861]. Floyd's crossing of the Gauley, the loss of his ferry-boat on August 23 and the Union concentration at Sutton are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the live field reads zero. Rosecrans relays Cox's reports that Tyler's Seventh Ohio, an advanced regiment, was surprised by Floyd with five regiments and three guns, the enemy estimated at 5,000 to 10,000. Wise gives Floyd's command as 2,600 men, less the sick and furloughed, and calls Tyler's regiment the enemy's whole advance guard.
claims.rationale: Second-hand estimates and a co-commander's itemized figure from October; no count of those engaged. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Brigadier General John Floyd and Colonel Erastus Tyler; the live page gives Tyler as Brigadier General. Rosecrans relays that the Seventh Ohio was under Tyler; Wise says Floyd ordered him to send regiments, that he withheld them pending further orders, and that Floyd surprised Tyler's regiment. Neither listed commander's own report is in the inspected volume.
claims.rationale: Command roles from relayed and retrospective accounts; no automatic sole credit and the live rank is not adopted.

open_questions: Floyd's and Tyler's own reports and Cox's dispatches are not in the inspected pages of Volume V; Floyd's and Wise's August correspondence (cited by Wise) and any later Official Records supplement remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Rosecrans's two August 28, 1861 telegrams relaying Cox (Official Records Series I, Volume V) are one family of interested Union accounts at second hand. Wise's October 26, 1861 report (same volume), written after his recall to answer Floyd, is one family of interested and polemical Confederate accounts; Wise was not at Cross-Lanes. The Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge. No Scribner Campaigns of the Civil War volume narrates this engagement; Nicolay's Chapter XII ends with McClellan's campaign in July.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
